verified: PlanePhysicsProbe.cs + tools/_probe_planephys.mjs -- 101 values across 5 synthetic contact cases (equal-mass head-on, heavy-vs-light, an off-centre glancing hit exercising both angular lever arms and friction, a separating contact that must return null, a pure sliding-friction contact), plus _damage at 4 energy/mass/colMult points and _restitution at 6 speeds. The JS side instantiates the REAL src/planephys.js PlanePhysics class (`new PlanePhysics({})` is safe -- its constructor touches nothing but `this.game = game`) and calls its own _solve/_damage/_restitution directly against synthetic actors satisfying the same duck-typed interface IPlanePhysicsActor formalises; this is not a reimplementation standing in for ground truth, it IS the shipped module. THREE REAL BUGS CAUGHT AND FIXED DURING AUTHORING, before any probe run (plain code review against the JS line-by-line): (1) the 'sits back on its wheels vs lies however it fell' branch in GroundContacts originally checked `OnHurt == null` -- a meaningless leftover -- instead of the JS's `!rec.dead`; fixed by adding a real Dead flag to LooseAirframeActor. (2) HandleHurtResult (the _hurt kill follow-up: fire, gear-fold, explosion cue, scatter) had no guard against an already-dead airframe, so every subsequent hit on a wreck would replay the explosion sound and re-run Scatter -- the JS's _hurt fully no-ops once rec.dead; fixed with an explicit Dead check using the OLD value before Kill() runs. (3) Torn (which part of the airframe has already come off) was declared but never actually populated, and Scatter()'s mass-loss reconciliation re-applied ApplyMassLoss to parts torn off in EARLIER, unrelated calls -- fixed by porting _tear's exact guard-on-attempt/mass-loss-only-on-success semantics as a shared Tear() helper used by both TearAt and Scatter. Separately, a leftover placeholder expression computed DamageToUs from a nonsensical always-null colMult lookup; fixed by adding a real ColMult field to PilotState.
